title: FAA issues US national ground stop on all flights
summary: "All ​departing traffic should remain groundstopped until further notice," the US Federal Aviation Administration said. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said technicians are investigating the issue.

title: Gambia's Adama Barrow seeks third term
summary: In tonight's programme, Gambia's electoral commission has announced the five official candidates for the country's upcoming presidential election. President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term. Tensions continue to rise in Ethiopia following the federal government's appointment of a new head of the Western Tigray region. And the Dakar Youth Olympic Games come to a close after two weeks of intense competition.

title: France among five major powers to represent EU in Ukraine talks
summary: European Council President Antonio Costa on Friday said that Brussels will send diplomats from the bloc and five countries, including the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, to upcoming Ukraine talks.

title: US flight authority orders national ground stop over air traffic control 'communication issue'
summary: The US flight authority on Friday halted flights across the nation due to what US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said was a communication issue affecting the country's air traffic control centres.

title: Tanker collides with New Orleans river cruise carrying 129 passengers, rescue operation underway
summary: A tanker struck and partially submerged a New Orleans river cruise carrying around 129 passengers. Multiple people were rescued as search-and-rescue operations continued.

title: Turkey and Qatar pledge unified stance against attacks in mutual defence pact
summary: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, the two leaders said in a joint statement. The defence pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.

title: The Downfall of AI’s ‘Rock Star’ Boss, Ukraine: Who speaks for Europe? Protests & Presidents
summary:
On The World This Week with Gavin Lee, our panel distills the breaking news and global stories of the past 7 days into 45 minutes. 
 
Ukraine: Who will speak for Europe?
 
In a week thats seen the first direct talks between Ukraine and Russia since February, with the US in the room and the Europeans relegated to the lobby according to Moscow. A new ‘European Security Architecture’ is discussed.

title: Ukraine updates: EU to send united front to potential peace talks
summary: Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland — as well as the EU itself — will jointly represent Europe in possible peace talks. Meanwhile, a second car bomb in two days has exploded in Moscow. DW has more.

title: David Walliams: UK police launch sex offense probe into comedian
summary: The "Little Britain" star and "Britain's Got Talent" judge has been accused of engaging in sexual misconduct and inappropriate behavior towards young women and girls. Walliams denies the allegations.

title: EU deal on Ukraine talks overshadows AI-focused summit in Dublin
summary: EU leaders have agreed that the E5 format — Germany, France, U.K, Italy and Poland — plus the European Commission and Council will represent the bloc at any future peace negotiations.

title: Hurry up and wait: Europe wants a place at the table, ‘must make up its mind’ over Ukraine
summary: Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Alexander Titov, Lecturer in Modern European History at Queen's University Belfast and a specialist on Russia. He's joined us to discuss high-level meetings in Abu Dhabi, Dublin and the prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.

title: EU leaders bring Italy and Poland into Ukraine peace talks team as Kallas fights for spot
summary: Europe has decided on a joint team for the peace talks led by France, Germany, the UK, Italy, Poland, the EU institutions and NATO. Despite mounting pressure, leaders declined to appoint a single envoy.

title: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
summary: China has been carrying out major military drills around Taiwan since early November. But contrary to some claims on social media, Beijing's armed forces have not actually implemented a blockade on the island; they just simulated it.

title: Why Europe failed to find a superhero to take on Putin
summary: Europe’s seven-part team of Ukraine peace envoys must now agree their strategy for handling Russia.

title: Le Pen offers to meet Zelenskyy in Brussels
summary: The Ukrainian leader wants to persuade the far-right leader to continue supporting Ukraine if she becomes president of France.

title: 'We have done all our homework' to get EU candidate status: Kosovo's PM Albin Kurti
summary: FRANCE 24 hosts Albin Kurti, the prime minister of Kosovo, a country that declared its independence from Serbia back in 2008 and sees itself as part of the European family. But four years after applying to join the EU, Kosovo has still not received candidate status. We explore Kosovo's path towards the EU, and the broader European and regional dynamics surrounding that.

title: Russia sends major business delegation to Kabul for business talks with the Taliban
summary: A Russian deputy prime minister led a 70-strong Russian delegation to Afghanistan, pursuing deals on transport, logistics, agriculture, and health products with the Taliban.

title: Microsoft outage renews European calls to detox from US tech
summary: Lawmakers across Europe call for action to reduce reliance on a handful of foreign tech companies.

title: The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
summary: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

title: As EU grapples with fierce AI competition, summit overshadowed by elusive Ukraine-Russia peace deal
summary: As EU leaders meet for an AI summit in Dublin, largely overshadowed by Russia's war on Ukraine, William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome Fabrice Pothier, CEO of Rasmussen Global. On AI, Pothier points to Europe's limited computing capacity, estimating that it barely represents "5% of what's available out there." Despite the EU's wealth of researchers and expertise, he warns that Europe is struggling to turn these resources into "real technological and industrial scale." Now, turning to the war in Ukraine, Pothier argues that European governments should focus less on "whether they have a place at the table" and more on "making Ukraine's hands stronger," particularly by providing additional air defence interceptors.

title: Iran MPs debate possible shift in nuclear doctrine and exit from NPT
summary: Although the US midterm elections result appears to have reduced for now the prospect of a new full-scale US and Israeli attack on Iran, the fundamental US objective of stopping any Iranian nuclear programme is generating an intense debate in the Iranian society and its power circles.

title: Berlin clan boss Issa Remmo appears as 'state guest' at EU Parliament event
summary: The head of the so-called Remmo clan in Berlin, Issa Remo, has officially joined a conference against Islamism in the European Parliament. This is fuelling debate in Germany and Brussels, and many are asking how this is possible.

title: The Nvidia affair: Are markets about to fall out of love with AI?
summary: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia exposes the vulnerabilities behind the AI boom. As equities reel in response to his resignation following extramarital affairs, alleged Chinese espionage and a summons to testify before US lawmakers, questions mount over who is really in charge of tech and whether the immense capital riding on it can survive the turmoil.

title: Latest news bulletin | November 13th, 2026 – Evening
summary: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 13th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

title: More live news, more conversations, more Europe: Euronews reinvents itself for its new season
summary:
Euronews launches its new season on 16 November with more live journalism, new weeknight programmes and a brand-new studio. Its journalists and editorial expertise take centre stage, with more perspectives and deeper insight into the stories shaping Europe.
 
More Europe than ever, in 12 languages.

title: November 13 Paris attacks: Eleven years later, France pays tribute to victims
summary: Eleven years on, France pays tribute to the victims of the November 13 attacks. French officials, victims’ associations and families gathered this Friday to pay their respects to those killed in the attacks in Paris on November 13, 2015.

title: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'
summary: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace. People taking it had to navigate extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. What has become of the road after the US-led war and five years of Taliban rule? Our former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to find out.

title: Myanmar: Junta carries out double-tap airstrikes targeting civilians
summary: Numerous civilian casualties have been documented in Rakhine State amid a renewed military offensive by the junta to regain control of the area.  Available evidence suggests that military aircraft are deliberately targeting civilian sites and carrying out double-tap strikes.

title: El Niño fuels climate disasters: The high price of inaction
summary: 2026 is set to be one of the hottest years on record, with El Niño worsening the impact of extreme weather events. With COP31 underway in Turkey, FRANCE 24 speaks with the UNDP's climate boss about the cost of waiting in a warmer world, and with one of the student activists from Pacific Island nations who took their climate fight to the UN's highest court, and won.

title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
summary: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

title: Ex-Labour MP accused of sexual harassment joins Plaid Cymru
summary: Geraint Davies has joined Wales' ruling party.

title: What Vladimir Putin won in Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks
summary: Donald Trump’s envoys offered the Russian president what he wants: room to stall.

title: West Bank: ‘Without international trade and financial support, large settlements would not exist’
summary: France is considering legislation to restrict trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, namely the West Bank. Ivar Ekeland, Professor Emeritus at Paris Dauphine-PSL University and Chair of the Organization of Academics for the Respect of International Law in Palestine, discusses the proposed measures with Alison Sargent. He calls for restrictions to cover n ot only goods but also services, including financial services, insurance and tourism. "Without the support of financial entities, of insurance, of providing goods and so on, settlements, big settlements, would not exist," he argues.

title: Ice hockey: Russia threatens against Canada and Germany over exclusion from tournaments
summary: A fortnight after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

title: UN refugee chief Barham Salih slams 'shameful' war in Sudan, urges 'political solution'
summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, UN refugee chief Barham Salih called the war in Sudan "shameful" and urged the world to end it. With forced displacement at a record high, he warned that funding cuts are hurting people "in dire need". "Efficiency has its limits," he said. Salih also defended the "integrity of the asylum system".

title: Nvidia scandal: How close was ex-CEO to Trump?
summary: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Just how close Huang was to Trump and the extent of the influence tech giants have on his administration are some of the questions that still need answering, says France 24’s Douglas Herbert.

title: Russia strikes targets across Ukraine as Kyiv launches nearly 1,200 drones
summary: Russian strikes hit targets across Ukraine on Thursday, with one attack damaging a hospital. Ukraine meanwhile fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.

title: Iran targeted US radar system in Bahrain
summary: Iran claimed it struck US radar systems in Bahrain, while the US said it had intercepted the attacks. Clashes continue in the Strait of Hormuz, as the war remains in a state of de-escalation.

title: Beijing faces its Russia dilemma amid talk of Xi-Trump-Putin summit
summary: China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. While the optics are sure to favor Moscow, Beijing is risking its image at the global stage.

title: Cyber attacks and hybrid warfare: Germany gives sweeping powers to its police and intelligence services
summary: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?

title: Azerbaijan intensifies its European engagement at the EPC Summit
summary: Azerbaijan added additional thrust to its engagement with Europe announcing more energy to the EU, a strategic partnership with the UK, additional agreements with Ukraine, a dozen bilateral meetings with European leaders and a new meeting with Armenia to advance the historic peace process.

title: Haitian forces recapture national stadium after two years of gang control
summary: Haitian security forces regained control Thursday, November 12, of the country's main stadium that had been under gang control for two years, forcing the national football team to play elsewhere. The Haitian National Police said in a statement that it had taken "full control" of the venue with the Task Force, a private security group serving the government, after which it left the stadium under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers.

title: Roger Waters launches heartfelt plea for 'an end to the genocide in Gaza'
summary: Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has always mixed art with activism. A long-standing supporter of the Palestinian cause, the star guitarist has now released a re-imagined version of the rock anthem "Comfortably Numb" with Palestinian American singer Mona Miari singing in Arabic. He tells FRANCE 24's Lyana Saleh why proceeds of the record are going to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund and why he can never become "Comfortably Numb" with the violence and suffering in Gaza.

title: 'Devastated wasteland': Haitian security forces regain control of stadium from gangs
summary: Haitian security forces said they have regained control of the country's main stadium, wresting it back from the gangs that have been using it for the past two years. They were assisted by the Task Force, a private security group serving the government. The stadium is now under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers. FRANCE 24's senior reporter Catherine Norris Trent, who has covered Haiti extensively, said re-taking the stadium would be a significant step in an area of the city that had been a "devastated wasteland".

title: Indonesia's wiretapping scandal opens a political fault line
summary: Senior police officers are accused of illegally monitoring President Prabowo Subianto, exposing rival networks within Indonesia's security establishment and renewing concerns about political misuse of surveillance.

title: The truth about Douma: How Syria covered up a chemical attack
summary: On April 7, 2018, the Syrian town of Douma, on the outskirts of the capital Damascus, was targeted by a chemical attack. Evidence pointed to the Syrian regime, yet proof vanished, and eyewitnesses went silent. Eight years later, FRANCE 24's Jenna Le Bras tracked down survivors and witnesses of the deadly attack. She also met representatives of some of the world's most powerful institutions to understand how a massive cover-up campaign had been orchestrated by the regime, with Russian support.

title: EU leaders discuss how to boost Europe's AI industry while tackling risks at Dublin summit
summary: European leaders together with Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch and AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton discussed how Europe can build its AI industry while making sure the technology is developed responsibly.

title: Kallas says 'Russians don't want me' as EU envoy for peace talks
summary: Kaja Kallas has made a strong push to be appointed special EU envoy for the peace negotiations. But "Russians do not want me", she added.

title: North Macedonia: Kriva Palanka seeks help over 1,000 free-roaming cows
summary: More than 1,000 cows are roaming freely through Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia, damaging property and alarming residents. The mayor wants the government to declare a 30-day state of crisis.

title: China warns US over chip curbs as suspected spy’s firm got banned chips
summary: The row threatens to overshadow next week’s expected Trump-Xi meeting, as Congress pushes for tougher limits on sales to Beijing.

title: Turkey: Six-metre Trojan Horse spills plastic waste at COP31
summary: A giant Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste has appeared in Antalya as Greenpeace International staged a striking environmental protest during the COP31 climate summit. Created with Danish artist Thomas Dambo, the Greenpeace installation warns of the environmental impact of plastics.

title: Microsoft 365 global outage disrupts Portuguese government, health services and schools
summary: A global failure in Microsoft services is disrupting several sectors in Portugal. The outage since Thursday affects Outlook and Teams, though the company reports progress in restoring access.

title: Rosalía's 'Lux' dominates Latin Grammys as Argentine artists shine
summary: The Catalan artist wins five of seven awards, including song and album of the year. Milo J's folk tribute triumphs, with 'Niño' best recording and nine more prizes for Argentines.

title: From Ukraine peace to Europe's future: How Russia is shifting the debate
summary: As talks to end Russia’s war in Ukraine make little progress, Moscow is pushing for a wider deal on Europe’s security, raising fears that the Kremlin is seeking to reshape the continent’s future on its own terms.

title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms has cast doubt on Anthropic's looming IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

title: Hungary’s MOL seeks EU funding as CEO warns Russian oil phase-out could trigger social unrest
summary: MOL says it could phase out Russian oil imports by the end of 2027, but chief Bacsa warns that higher energy costs could fuel political instability in Hungary and Slovakia. He is calling for EU funding to expand alternative pipeline routes, as Brussels keeps focus on quitting Russian energy.

title: At least three killed and more than 20 injured in Russian strikes on Ukraine
summary: It comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrapped up a meeting with US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Ireland on Thursday.

title: Debate: What does the resignation of Nvidia CEO Huang mean?
summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his post following the revelations about his affair with a suspected Chinese spy. After he admitted to the liaison on Sunday, the media reported that Huang had also had affairs with two female employees. Since the scandal broke, Nvidia, which is the world's largest chip manufacturer, has seen its market capitalisation plunge by around 800 billion dollars. Commentators discuss the many aspects of the affair.

title: Back to the Cold War | Blog Damijan - Slovenia
Conspiracy theorists can pack their bags | Ilya Ber - Russia
Debate: Ukraine negotiations: reshuffling the deck in Europe?
summary: This week's Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi have ended without a major breakthrough. The heads of state and government attending the European Political Community (EPC) summit in Dublin on Thursday discussed further support for Ukraine. The US has held out the prospect of European involvement in future negotiations. Russia is calling for a comprehensive agreement on the European security architecture.

title: No one can trust Moscow anymore | Ilia Matveev - Russia
Debate: Coalition in The Hague divided over wealth tax
summary: A split within Prime Minister Rob Jetten's three-party minority coalition government is looming in the Netherlands. The bone of contention is a key point in the planned tax reform: Jetten's D66 party passed the 'millionaire tax', which increases taxes for wealthy individuals, with the support of the red-green opposition party Pro, but against the wishes of its right-wing liberal coalition partner, the VVD. The VVD then withdrew its support for the tax reform as a whole.

title: Debate: Turkey: why is the peace process with the PKK stalling?
summary: Just under two years after PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan called for the organisation to be disbanded, the peace process in Turkey appears to be losing momentum. President Erdoğan has urged patience. İbrahim Kalın, head of the country's National Intelligence Organisation, has blamed the PKK's leadership for the delays, but also called on Ankara to introduce democratic reforms.

title: European diesel prices stay high as global oil supply overtakes demand, IEA says
summary: European diesel prices are still 77% above pre-war levels, the IEA said on Friday. Global oil supplies are expected to exceed demand in the fourth quarter as Gulf exports recover.

title: China to encourage investment in Turkish renewable energy with $15bn solar and wind deal
summary: Türkiye wants to sharply expand solar and wind power by 2040 and is seeking foreign investment to fund the work.

title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Club Kid' - Sex, drugs & sudden parenthood
summary: A gay party promoter is suddenly faced with fatherhood in a familiar but engaging debut from Jordan Firstman, who ensures you'll be charmed and (nearly) moved to tears.

summary: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 13th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

title: How a new ‘green energy corridor’ from the Caspian Sea could help Eastern Europe kick fossil fuels
summary: The partnership signed at the COP31 climate summit aims to transform Azerbaijan into an interregional electricity hub.

title: Darth Vader's lightsaber breaks Star Wars auction record by selling for nearly €4.5 million
summary: Auctioneers estimated the on screen prop would sell for over $1m, but the lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the famous “I am your father” scene ended up selling for nearly $5m.

title: Ukraine: Russian drone attacks hit Kyiv hospital, leave two dead in Odesa
summary: Russian overnight attacks on Ukraine killed at least two person in Odesa and injured another at a hospital in Kyiv. Rescuers evacuated patients, including people using wheelchairs and crutches, as firefighters battled the flames.

title: ExxonMobil sues EU over rules forcing oil giants to invest in carbon storage
summary: US oil giant ExxonMobil is challenging EU rules requiring fossil fuel producers to help fund carbon storage infrastructure, in a legal battle that could undermine Brussels’ efforts to make the industry pay for the energy transition.

title: Why the UK wants to jail undersea cable saboteurs and why tougher punishment may not be enough
summary: The United Kingdom is seeking tougher penalties for damaging critical underwater infrastructure, but industry insiders warn that stronger rules alone cannot prevent widespread disruption.

title: Microsoft outage explained: what went wrong and is your data at risk?
summary: Governments, doctor surgeries and even rival AI firms have been caught up, and the episode is sharpening questions about Europe's reliance on a handful of US tech giants.

title: US denies IRGC destroyed American radar in Bahrain after attack on southern Iran
summary: Despite rising military tensions, diplomatic efforts mediated by Qatar and Pakistan are continuing. Tehran has made any resumption of formal negotiations with Washington conditional on its demands being met.

title: Humanitarian situation in Gaza worsens amid political deadlock
summary: In war-battered Gaza, heavy rain flooded and damaged thousands of tents. Several people died. Could pressure by Trump's Board of Peace on Israel and Hamas help to ease the humanitarian crisis amid stalled peace talks?

title: José Pinhal's rediscovered songs sell out Porto and Lisbon Coliseums
summary: A tribute band to an artist who was only known in an ultra-restricted circle while alive sent the Coliseu dos Recreios wild at its farewell concert. Understanding the José Pinhal phenomenon means grasping our century's drive to reclaim nuggets from the past.

title: Swedish pop sensation Robyn brands Eurovision ‘embarrassing’
summary: Swedish pop star Robyn, whose hits include 'With Every Heartbeat' and 'Dancing On My Own', shared her verdict on Eurovision during an appearance on Amy Poehler's podcast. She suggested Eurovision's appeal had diminished for her since ABBA’s involvement, and that it was "embarrassing".

title: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget
summary: The budget committee in the Bundestag worked into the night to sign off on next year's spending plans. These include levels of new debt only eclipsed once, at the height of the COVID pandemic. DW has more.

title: Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
summary: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.

title: After suffering its worst election result, what's next for the ANC — and for South Africa?
summary: A crushing local election result across the country has left South Africa's ruling ANC searching for answers. Experts say the vote reflects public frustration with service delivery failures — signaling a political shift.

title: Portugal: Humanoid robots take centre stage at Web Summit 2026
summary: Dancing humanoid robots and robotic dogs stole the show at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon. The technology conference has generated nearly €2.5 billion for Portugal's economy over the past decade, according to a study.

title: Flying Blue flies high: These are the best airline rewards programmes in Europe
summary: Air France-KLM's Flying Blue was crowned the best frequent flyer scheme globally thanks to how easy it is to earn and spend miles. The British Airways Club and Virgin Atlantic Flying Club also ranked high.

title: 'The market will look for alternatives,' on Huang resignation says Andrea Renda, Digital Economy expert
summary: Nvidia is at the centre of the global artificial intelligence revolution. But the American chip giant is now facing an extraordinary crisis, following the shock resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of an espionage scandal.

title: 'The structure of the European economy needs to change more quickly,' says IMF Europe chief Mateusz Szczurek
summary: Europe's economy is facing a dangerous combination of challenges: sluggish growth, mounting public debt and rising borrowing costs. As sovereign bond yields put pressure on government finances, Europe's ability to invest in its future is increasingly in question.

title: European shares fall as Nvidia CEO’s exit raises doubts over AI boom
summary: Equity markets mostly fell on Friday, following losses on Wall Street as investors weighed what Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia could mean for the AI industry. Oil prices rose after US President Donald Trump said Washington did not need a deal with Iran.

title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
summary: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.

title: US pushes for European presence at Ukraine-Russia talks, which Moscow refuses to confirm
summary: "Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners," US special envoy Jared Kushner said. Moscow has not confirmed whether it has agreed to include European negotiators in subsequent talks.

title: EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
summary: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

title: Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
summary: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

title: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
summary: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

title: Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
summary: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

title: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
summary: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

title: What are fossil fuels?
summary: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

title: Germany news: Police raid chapters of Gremium MC biker gang
summary: Police in southwestern Germany launched major early-morning operations against a biker gang. The state of Baden-Württemberg is outlawing three of its chapters. Meanwhile, unions are planning more strikes.

title: Bundeswehr study exposes widespread sexual harassment in German military
summary: Sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known, with younger women disproportionately affected. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has called for a policy of "zero tolerance."

title: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge
summary: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
summary: The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
summary: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
summary: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
summary: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
summary: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
summary: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
summary: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

title: Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
summary: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
summary: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

title: Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
summary: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
summary: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
summary: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

title: US, Russia, Ukraine wrap up talks with prisoner exchange agreement
summary: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
summary: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.
